subject: Tethys variant intake — provisional pin and compatibility coordination
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@datascale.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: New model intake: Tethys-3B — compatibility check request

Hi Stephanie / Laura,

Thanks again for taking a look. We're evaluating Redwood for serving Tethys-3B (open checkpoint) and wanted to start the intake/compatibility conversation. Initial notes: the vendor optimized the tokenizer (subword variant) and the model was trained with a slight KV cache layout tweak that changed past-key ordering for long-context use cases.

Attachments: tethys_model_card.pdf, compat_report_v1.csv (small infra-run with sample prompts)

As a next step, could you confirm whether Redwood would need a provisional pin or a temporary compatibility window to validate tokenization and KV ordering? Our SRE is asking about a canary that will run for ~48 hours before production traffic.

High level asks from DataScale:
- A short list of required artifacts we should prepare (weights format, tokenizer files, sample prompts)
- Whether any model-variant fallbacks would be required to prevent regressions
- Expected timeline for a staged ingress (canary -> ramp)

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of ML Infrastructure, DataScale Inc.
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@datascale.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-24T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: New model intake: Tethys-3B — compatibility check request

Sara — thanks for the details and the artifacts. Looping in Laura for intake (model gating) and Aditya + Priyom for the technical compatibility assessment and rollout planning. A few immediate asks from our side:

- Please confirm exact tokenizer files (vocab, merges/bpe config). If you have a tokenization test vector (text -> token ids) include that in the archive.
- Include a minimal weights export (float16 / quantized if available) plus the model config and example generation seed.

Aditya / Laura / Priyom, quick question for the intake: based on Sara's note about KV ordering changes, do we want to request a provisional pin (prevent new variant from being auto-selected) while we validate? If so, propose what scope and duration (48h canary sounds reasonable, but we may need 1-week provisional pin to run embedding/regression checks).

I like to avoid a hard block unless safety or correctness regressions are likely. Can the team do an initial compatibility pass within 48 business hours and advise whether a pin is needed? If pinning is required, recommend an explicit rollback/fallback variant and telemetry signals to watch.

Happy to take this through normal intake but wanted to surface the ask early because DataScale is targeting an end-of-month pilot.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
VP, Product
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, sara@datascale.ai
Date: 2027-10-24T15:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: New model intake: Tethys-3B — compatibility check request

Stephanie / Team / Sara,

Quick technical readout from the preliminary sandbox run (see compat_report_v1.csv, summarized below):

Findings:
- Tokenization: The vendor's tokenizer produces a different token id sequence for a handful of anchor prompts vs. our baseline tokenizers (off-by-1 ids on rare unicode sequences). That suggests we need the exact tokenizer artifacts; otherwise we risk generation drift.
- KV layout: The KV cache uses a different past-key concatenation order for blocks > 2048 tokens. In our runtime that shows up as shifted attention in long-chat transcripts. Short-form generation (<=512 tokens) looks functionally identical.
- Quantization: We tested float16 and 8-bit dynamic quant; no immediate accuracy cliff, but perplexity varies on some safety prompts.

Recommendation:
1) Provisional pin the Tethys-3B variant in intake for an initial 7-day window ("provisional_pin: 7d"). Rationale: the tokenizer mismatch plus KV ordering only shows up under long contexts; a 48h canary may miss regression patterns in longer dialogue workloads.
2) Run a staged canary plan during the pin: 24h short-form canary, then 72h long-context stress with playback dataset from DataScale. If we observe drift on our evaluation prompts, we move to fallback variant "tethys-v2-compat" (the vendor gave a compatibility build) automatically.
3) Ask DataScale to provide: tokenizer test vectors, a fixed seed sample, and the earliest-minimal weights export. Also request a signed model card highlighting KV layout differences.

Attachments included: tokenizer-diff.patch (small script showing token-id differences), compat_report_v1.csv

I can lead the sandbox runs and produce the gating checklist within 48 business hours if we agree to the 7-day provisional pin.

-Aditya
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: sara@datascale.ai, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: New model intake: Tethys-3B — compatibility check request

Thanks Aditya -- this plan sounds sensible. From a rollout and product perspective I propose the following narrow scope so we can support DataScale's pilot while containing risk:

1) Provisional pin window: 7 days (as Aditya proposed) with an automatic extension option if we need more telemetry.
2) Canary staging: low qps canary in dedicated staging pool -> staggered ramp to a small % of production (2-5%) in Dedicated/Demo orgs only; do not expose to hosted API default routing.
3) Telemetry gates: token-mismatch rate, generation-embedding drift, safety-check fails. Aditya to provide thresholds; suggestion: token-mismatch > 0.2% or embedding cosine drop > 0.05 triggers immediate rollback.
4) Communication: We'll add a short mutual action plan doc and a DocuSign approval for the provisional pin. Sara, can you confirm the playback dataset and sign-off owner?

If everyone agrees, Stephanie, can you approve the provisional pin so Aditya can start runs and Laura can mark the variant as "provisionally_locked" in the intake tracker? I will draft the MAP and DocuSign link.

--Priyom
Product Manager, Model Intake
Redwood Inference
